In one sentence: The powers that be in F1 right now are getting together to re-write some of the most fundamental rules of the sport to bring in a new era with faster, louder, more powerful, and more aggressive-looking cars; all while encouraging closer, more exciting racing.

It all goes back to what sets apart Formula One from other kinds of Top-Tier racing like NASCAR and IndyCar. In those series, every team and driver is given basically the same car with the same (or very similar) engine and are told to go race them. In F1, you have a regulatory body that gives constructors (the teams) and engine manufacturers a set of rules and parameters that they must stay within and then they are told to build cars and engines as best they can within those rules.

In decades past (to some, "the golden years" of F1) this resulted in wildly different cars and crazy racing. Unfortunately, because of the influence of BIG money and politics in the sport, this hasn't been the case in recent years. This is not to say that the racing has been uninteresting or even boring, far from it - over the last 4 years we've seen some of the most exciting racing and driver rivalries of all time - but the overall feel among the fans and most of the people within the sport is that it could be much, much better.

Having said that, it would be fantastic for you if you got into F1 at this point because things are looking up and it's only going to get better. We'd love it if you want to give our podcast a shot, I would say wait till our next podcast, we are recording it tomorrow and should be out by the end of the day, and we will make a point to go over a few things from a new fan's perspective. If you give it a chance, you'll see that F1 is not like any other sport you've seen, not even like any other kind of racing for that matter.

The people on the pitwall and the strategists all want to desperately prove their worth and get a succes. This can lead to either overthinking or underthinking certain elemants of a race or a strategy.

The pressure they feel to make the right decision at the right time is why they get paid the big bucks, but sometimes this pressure makes for a bad call. It's not the end of the world, its racing.

Its too easy to criticize decisions that have to be made in the heat of the moment with imperfect information and in changing circumstances.

I would've liked to see Williams let Bottas race Massa but I understand the decision to hold station. It's not hard to run off your tires trying to get past someone, let alone have a coming together.
